claims.text: A hybrid CALPHAD–machine-learning framework will accurately predict melting temperatures for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework will accurately predict entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Experimental melting data for refractory MPEAs above 2000 °C are sparse or unreliable.
A thermodynamic dataset containing 355 MPEA compositions is available for model training.
Canonical correlation analysis and genetic algorithms can be used to identify useful descriptors for screening MPEAs.
Mean melting temperature and mean bulk modulus are influential descriptors for HEA phase formation.
Calibration against CALPHAD phase diagrams will enable prediction of both solidus temperature and entropy of fusion.
The intended domain includes equimolar combinations of three to six elements drawn from 26 metallic elements, calculations from 600 °C to 3600 °C, and systems with fAB equal to 1.
The cited screening domain also establishes coverage of non-equiatomic combinations.
Configurational entropy rises as ln(N) with the number of principal elements.
The number of binary interactions rises as (N/2)(N−1).
Increasing configurational entropy and the number of binary interactions drive a transition from solid solutions to intermetallics and produce a nonlinear composition–property relationship.
Rule-of-mixtures methods fail for these alloys because they assume linear additivity and cannot capture complex thermodynamic interactions.
The median Gibbs energy of intermetallic compounds in HEAs is approximately −36 kJ mol−1.
Intermetallic compounds generally have very small, often zero, formation entropies, and these quantities dominate their stability.
Machine learning can learn a nonlinear mapping between melting-point and bulk-modulus descriptors and HEA phase stability.
The method is valid only for systems with three to six principal elements and fully assessed binary interaction data, fAB equal to 1.
The melting-temperature model will achieve a correlation coefficient greater than 0.79.
Formation enthalpy of intermetallic compounds is essential to phase stability but difficult to estimate because no general model is available.
Vibrational formation entropy is generally an order of magnitude smaller than configurational entropy in concentrated solid-solution alloys.
